title: SDK transport safety layer: adaptive deadlines and socket reap policy
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see customer support cases where long-tail requests or heavy connection churn result in either inflated latency (customers set overly conservative per-request timeouts) or resource pressure (too many idle sockets kept open). Goal: provide a cross-SDK safety layer that (1) applies adaptive request deadlines driven by route-level SLOs and recent latency distributions, and (2) introduces a lease-based socket reap policy that stops idle sockets from accumulating while preserving warm-connection benefits for bursty workloads. This ticket covers API ergonomics and reference examples across Python/TS/Go, telemetry hooks, and a rollout plan that is backwards-compatible.

Scope and non-goals: implement SDK-side logic and examples; runtime/server changes are out-of-scope except for relying on existing route SLO metadata exposed via header/handshake. We will not change default keepalive OS settings; instead expose conservative, safe defaults with config overrides.

Success criteria:
- New SDK config keys available in Python/TS/Go with identical semantics.
- Adaptive deadline decreases 95th percentile customer-visible timeout-related errors by 30% in our staging load tests for chat/generation routes.
- Socket reap reduces idle connection count in integration harness by 40% without measurable latency regression for common burst patterns.
- Telemetry emitted for decisions (deadline applied, socket reaped, preserve-reuse event) and shipped documentation + examples.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Nina Patel: Initial ticket. Collected examples from existing SDK telemetry and support triage. Proposed knobs: adaptive_deadline.enabled, adaptive_deadline.base_ms, adaptive_deadline.max_ms, keepalive.idle_reap_ms, keepalive.probe_interval_ms, connection.max_age_ms, connection.lease_recycle_ratio.

2026-02-24 - Liam Chen: Spike complete. Reproduced idle-socket growth with bursty integration test. Implemented a PoC in TypeScript: adaptive deadline uses exponentially weighted moving average of p50/p95 to pick deadline = clamp(base, p95 * 1.25, max). Observed 25% fewer timeout escalations in PoC. Sharing PoC branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 (WIP).

2026-03-01 - Alice Romero (Product): Reviewed trade-offs. Important to keep defaults completely non-disruptive: adaptive_deadline.enabled=false by default for GA, but will enable in runtime experiments for select beta customers. Need docs and console flag to opt-in.

2026-03-05 - Security review note (Samir Khan): No secret surface changes. Telemetry events will include only numeric latencies and coarse decision tags; ensure IPs and tokens never emitted. Keeper: security sign-off required before enabling default=true.

2026-03-08 - Liam Chen: Implemented keepalive reap in Go SDK PoC. Lease recycling: when connection count > target, oldest idle connections are reaped with backoff per host. Added metrics: sdk.transport.reap.count, sdk.transport.reap.latency_impact_ms. Observed 42% drop in idle sockets on staging harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/213

2026-03-10 - Design review (Maya Ortiz): UX note for console: expose per-route advisory graph showing expected deadline vs applied deadline and a toggle for enabling adaptive deadlines per project. Adding follow-up PM ticket to own console surface.
implementation_notes: Cross-SDK implementation plan: 1) common semantics doc + unit-test vectors; 2) implement core algorithm in TypeScript runtime module and port to Python/Go with identical math; 3) add telemetry events and feature flag gating; 4) compatibility tests (old client + new runtime, new client + old runtime); 5) beta rollout to 5 internal customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive reaping could degrade tail latency for bursty apps. Mitigation: conservative defaults, lease_recycle_ratio, and canary with traffic mirroring before enabling wide release.

Risk: Different SDK runtimes compute EMA differently leading to drift. Mitigation: publish exact math and test vectors; include a small compatibility header when clients make calls indicating algorithm version.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample decisions at 1% by default and provide a toggle for higher fidelity in enterprise plans.
follow_up_tasks: PM: Create console feature flag and per-route advisory surface (see Maya's comment).
QA: Add regression tests for streaming reconnect and resumable KV cache semantics under reaped sockets.
DS: Validate p95-based multiplier with customer workloads and propose adjusted multiplier if needed.
DevOps: Prepare rollout playbook and runbook entries for socket exhaustion/increased 5xx after rollout.
